service_note: A temporary release-candidate deployment, deleted after this acceptance. Not the public demo, which stayed on v1.1.1 throughout and served its own five-run daily allowance from a separate key in the same shared store.
question: How does a large language model differ from a neural network?
question_note: Chosen because v1.1.x answered it badly: the pipeline published claims that were entailed by their evidence and did not address the comparison. It is the case the answer contract and the relevance gate exist for.

public_limits_in_force.note: Identical to the public demo's per-run ceilings. Only the daily admission count differs: 30 // 30 = 1 rather than 150 // 30 = 5.

verifier.shared_with: the public demo, which uses the same endpoint and revision

quota.store: shared with the public demo (Render permits one free Key Value instance per workspace)
quota.isolation_note: The namespace is the only thing separating the two daily counters. It was verified against /api/readiness before the run rather than read from the dashboard.
quota.cap_verified: A second request after this run was refused 429 at the quota gate, before any provider call, so it spent nothing. The daily admission of one is enforced, not merely configured.

capture.method: raw bytes streamed to disk, timing recorded in a separate index
capture.note: Derived files were built offline from these bytes by the same tool. No second run was performed, and none could be: the daily allowance was one.

cost.openai_dashboard_charge_usd: not reconciled; the owner can read it from the provider dashboard for 2026-09-29
cost.huggingface_billed_usd: not measured; billed per hour of endpoint uptime, not per request
